questions.question: Which files remain allowed after merging the project and task contracts in the demo?
options: Every project-wide path plus every task-specific path.
Only documentation paths, because code files are always hard-blocked.
The intersection: `app.py` and `test_app.py`.
Only `scripts/release.sh`, because the project contract owns releases.
questions.explanation: `merge_contracts` intersects the two `allowed_files` sets. Both contracts permit `app.py` and `test_app.py`, so those are the effective allowed paths.

questions.question: What network egress survives the demo's contract merge?
options: Both `api.openai.com` and `api.anthropic.com`.
No network hosts, because any child list denies all traffic.
Only `evil.example` from the creep run.
The intersection, `api.anthropic.com`.
questions.explanation: The project allowlist contains two hosts and the child allowlist contains only `api.anthropic.com`; `_merge_egress` intersects them.

questions.question: What does `scope_check` report for the clean run?
options: `passed=True` and `over_budget=False` with no findings.
`passed=False` because every task must touch a documentation file.
`passed=False` because the task has a 30-minute budget.
`passed=True` but with a forbidden-write block for `app.py`.
questions.explanation: The clean run touches only effective allowed files, runs the acceptance command, stays within 30 minutes, and uses the allowlisted host, so no finding is emitted.

questions.question: How is `README.md` classified in the creep run?
options: A block-severity forbidden write.
An informational soft off-scope documentation write.
An in-scope write because README is in every allowed set.
It is ignored because only source files are examined.
questions.explanation: `README.md` matches `docs_paths_soft` and not the hard allowed/forbidden patterns, so it appears in `soft_off_scope_writes` with an `info` finding.

questions.question: Which creep-run path creates a `scope.forbidden` block?
options: `README.md`
`app.py`
`scripts/release.sh`
`test_app.py`
questions.explanation: The project contract forbids `scripts/release.sh`; the task contract additionally forbids `migrations/**`, so both appear as forbidden writes in the creep report.

questions.question: What is `creep_report.over_budget` in the demo?
options: `True`, because every informational finding consumes the violation budget.
`True`, because the elapsed time is over 30 minutes.
`True`, because the network host is not allowlisted.
`False`; the report has no warn-severity findings, even though block findings make `passed()` false.
questions.explanation: `over_budget` counts only findings with severity `warn`; the creep report has blocks and an info finding, so its warn count is zero while `passed()` is still false.
